Thank you for taking the time to leave feedback. I’m sorry that your experience has led you to feel this way.

General practice across the NHS is currently facing very high demand, and like many surgeries we use an online request system so that patients can tell us what they need and a clinician can review and prioritise requests safely. This helps ensure that urgent problems are identified quickly and that patients are directed to the most appropriate clinician or service.

The message you refer to about the practice being at safe capacity is not intended to dismiss patients. It is used when the number of clinical requests already received that day means we cannot safely take on additional cases without risking delays for those who may be seriously unwell. In those circumstances, local NHS guidance is to signpost patients to NHS 111 or urgent care services so they can still access timely help.

We do appreciate that this can feel frustrating, particularly if you were hoping to speak to someone directly. Our reception and care-navigation team do speak to patients every day and help many people who contact us by phone or in person, but the online system allows clinicians to triage requests more safely and fairly when demand is high.

If you would like us to look into your experience in more detail, please contact our team directly via the practice website or by speaking with reception so we can review what happened and see whether anything could have been handled differently.

Your feedback is important and helps us continue improving the service we provide to patients.",null,[0,119]]]],[null,null,null,["https://www.google.com/maps/reviews/data=!4m8!14m7!1m6!2m5!1sCi9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2xGMVYyVkNkSGxIY0RjeFNEQmlkVUY0YkRBMFZXYxAB!2m1!1s0x0:0xbe25b4c3d12354be!3m1!1s2@1:CAIQACodChtycF9oOlF1V2VCdHlHcDcxSDBidUF4bDA0VWc%7C%7C?hl=en"],["https://www.google.com/local/content/rap/report?postId=Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2xGMVYyVkNkSGxIY0RjeFNEQmlkVUY0YkRBMFZXYxAB&t=1&-KgswZGdtd0JoZ0VpTA&wv=1&d=286732320",null,null,"0ahUKEwiSnce21bKTAxU6OXsEHcdrOKIQoykIBygB"],null,[null,[[1,0]]]],"0ahUKEwiSnce21bKTAxU6OXsEHcdrOKIQ0pMFCAUoAQ"],null,"CAESYENBRVFBaHBDUTJrNFNVRlNTVzVEWjI5QlVEY3lSMDFqUlVSWmFGOWZSV2hEV1RSZlVHOVJhbWMyWTNKS2VIUkZTVUZCUVVGQlIyZG1YMEZ0VFdORlJGbG9SMEZCYVVGQg=="],[["Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25kV04yaG9aRVE1ZWxjeExXNUxUa1ZoUlhwcFdWRRAB",["0x0:0xbe25b4c3d12354be",null,1773082666660150,1773082666660150,[null,null,["https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/111549826438705021323/reviews?hl=en"],null,null,["Mick Powell","https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocL8JF3CbtrRqcFcJ4i1FD8u9sdhhPJj3aRIkyJVYhU9lASFkw=s120-c-rp-mo-br100",["https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/111549826438705021323?hl=en"],"111549826438705021323",null,1,0,null,[0,2,1],1,["1 review",null,null,null,null,[null,"0ahUKEwiSnce21bKTAxU6OXsEHcdrOKIQ7LoGCAkoAA"]]]],null,"a week ago",null,null,null,null,null,null,["Google","https://www.gstatic.com/images/branding/product/1x/googleg_48dp.png",null,null,5],null,1],[[5],null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,["en"],[["I have seen four GPs over the past few months, they have all been friendly, kind & helpful, explaining things that I needed help with &, taking time to do this. I was wrong.

If you want a GP surgery that delays appointments, fails to carry out requested tests by it's own GP's, and sends confusing messages asking for samples no clinician has actually requested, then HMG is the place for you. These errors cause weeks of delays and, in our case, left a young autistic child in pain for months.

Requests to see or speak to a doctor are routinely denied. Communication is strictly one‑way and always on their terms. If you or your child require reasonable adjustments or additional support, don’t expect them to be offered—because they won’t be. Poor practice is standard throughout.

Even when the complaints team is supposedly involved, don’t expect to hear anything. Messages can be passed to them, but even if they are already “looking into it,” you’ll be met with silence. Any adjustments they recommend are ignored by the clinicians anyway. It genuinely feels as though HMG considers itself above the Equality Act 2010.

Be prepared to chase constantly for updates, appointments, and answers. It’s normal to spend hours going back and forth with a receptionist—only to be told you need an emergency appointment that same day… and then be informed there are none available.

Referrals? Expect delays. Expect to be told things are “in progress” when they aren’t. Expect your child’s case to be passed around, lost in the system, and restarted again and again. Even when you find a staff member who genuinely wants to help, they hit the same wall of red tape and broken processes.

Don’t be reassured by messages like:
“Thank you for your contact. We have requested advice from the clinician whose care you are under. We will contact you as soon as we receive a response.”
Even when the issue is urgent, you’ll wait days for a reply and then another week before anyone can book you in with the named clinician. And if you want to switch clinicians? You’ll need to file a complaint, wait for an investigation, and hope someone eventually approves it.

Even when an external professional identifies potentially dangerous errors, the practice still refuses to speak to you. The lack of accountability is staggering.

The saddest part is that the staff who do care are held back by a system that simply doesn’t work. As someone who was a patient before the merger, I can honestly say it was the worst thing that could have happened to this practice.

If you want delays, confusion, denied access to doctors, ignored adjustments, and a system that leaves children suffering, then this “super” surgery is the one for you.",null,[0,143]]]],[null,1773216948000000,1773216948000000,"a week ago",null,"https://business.google.com/local/business/13999948025121986313/customers/reviews/reply?p=CkRDaTlEUVVsUlFVTnZaRU5vZEhsalJqbHZUMnBTTlZGdVNsWmtNRGx2V1d0c1VWbFZlRVpoTUVaNlZGaHdNbFpYWXhBQhAA",[null,null,null,"/local/business/13999948025121986313/customers/reviews/reply?p=CkRDaTlEUVVsUlFVTnZaRU5vZEhsalJqbHZUMnBTTlZGdVNsWmtNRGx2V1d0c1VWbFZlRVpoTUVaNlZGaHdNbFpYWXhBQhAA"],"https://business.google.com/local/business/13999948025121986313/customers/reviews/deletereply?p=CkRDaTlEUVVsUlFVTnZaRU5vZEhsalJqbHZUMnBTTlZGdVNsWmtNRGx2V1d0c1VWbFZlRVpoTUVaNlZGaHdNbFpYWXhBQhAA",[null,null,null,"/local/business/13999948025121986313/customers/reviews/deletereply?p=CkRDaTlEUVVsUlFVTnZaRU5vZEhsalJqbHZUMnBTTlZGdVNsWmtNRGx2V1d0c1VWbFZlRVpoTUVaNlZGaHdNbFpYWXhBQhAA"],null,"https://business.google.com/local/business/13999948025121986313/customers/reviews/reply?p=CkRDaTlEUVVsUlFVTnZaRU5vZEhsalJqbHZUMnBTTlZGdVNsWmtNRGx2V1d0c1VWbFZlRVpoTUVaNlZGaHdNbFpYWXhBQhAA",[null,null,null,"/local/business/13999948025121986313/customers/reviews/reply?p=CkRDaTlEUVVsUlFVTnZaRU5vZEhsalJqbHZUMnBTTlZGdVNsWmtNRGx2V1d0c1VWbFZlRVpoTUVaNlZGaHdNbFpYWXhBQhAA"],null,["en"],[["Dear Nikki

Thank you for taking the time to leave a review. We are very sorry to read how frustrated and concerned you feel about the care your child received. Any suggestion that a child has been left in pain or that processes have not worked as they should is something we take extremely seriously.

It would not be appropriate for us to discuss the details of any individual patient’s care in a public forum such as Google, particularly where children are involved. However, we can reassure you that we have clear systems for managing test requests, referrals, reasonable adjustments and safeguarding concerns, and we work within national NHS guidance and legal duties, including those set out in the Equality Act 2010.

Our teams deal with a very high volume of patient contacts every day, and while many patients tell us they receive timely and supportive care, we recognise that when communication or processes fall short the impact can be very frustrating. We continually review feedback and complaints so that we can improve how our systems work for patients and families.

If you have an open complaint with the practice, it will be reviewed through our formal complaints process and you will receive a response directly. If you would like us to look again at any aspect of your child’s care or ensure we have the correct reasonable adjustments recorded, we would strongly encourage you to contact the practice management team so we can review this with the relevant clinicians.

We are committed to providing safe, equitable care to all patients, including children and those who require additional support, and we would welcome the opportunity to look into your concerns properly rather than through a public review.

Thank you for sharing your feedback about the waiting time for a routine appointment. I understand that waiting for six weeks can be frustrating, and I want to provide some clarity on why this might be happening under our total triage system.  
Total triage is designed to ensure that every patient receives the most appropriate care based on their clinical needs. In responding to this comment, I have not looked at your individual record as I cannot comment on this forum.  However, I would like to assure you that the information that you submitted about the reasons that you need an appointment will have been reviewed by an experienced GP. They will have decided on the priority of your appointment based on these comments. 
Here's how it works:
1.	Prioritisation of Urgent Cases: Our triage system allows us to assess the urgency of each patient's needs. This means that patients with urgent or more severe conditions are prioritised and seen more quickly. As a result, routine or non-urgent appointments may have longer wait times.
2.	Efficient Use of Resources: By directing patients to the right healthcare professional or service, we aim to use our resources efficiently. This ensures that GPs and other clinicians can focus on patients who need their expertise the most, which can sometimes lead to longer waits for less urgent cases.
3.	High Demand and Limited Capacity: Like many practices, we face high demand for appointments and have a limited number of clinicians available. This can contribute to longer waiting times, especially during peak periods. Unfortunately, the funding that general practice is given is not unlimited so it is not always possible to increase the number of clinicians available. 
4.	Safety Netting and Alternative Services: While waiting for an appointment, we provide safety netting advice and may suggest alternative services, such as NHS 111 or local pharmacies, for issues that can be managed elsewhere.
Like you, we would like to see a shorter wait for routine appointments.  We are continuously working to improve our systems and reduce waiting times while ensuring that all patients receive safe and effective care.  
If your condition changes or you feel your needs are more urgent, please do not hesitate to contact us again.

Regards

My parents and I are all registered with them, and our experiences have been consistently disappointing.

Starting with my own case: a few months ago, I had two scans done. I had to wait over a month just to receive the results, and when I finally had an appointment to discuss them, I was told I could only review one scan because the doctor did not have time to go over both. Ridiculous!

It is deeply concerning that general practitioners are expected to interpret results they are not specialised in. Patients deserve to be seen by professionals who can accurately assess findings and offer appropriate treatment.

I refused to wait for my symptoms to worsen, so I went to a private clinic instead — where the issue was quickly identified, explained, and treated professionally.

Blood tests were carried out, and the results clearly showed concerning abnormalities in her liver function. Despite this, the doctors did not treat the findings as serious or take any urgent action.

Her pain worsened to the point where she had to go to A&E. There, a CT scan was performed, and it confirmed that her cancer had returned and spread.

We filed a formal complaint with HMG regarding the failure to act on the test results and the lack of urgency in her care. The response we received stated that the doctors did not view the liver results as an emergency requiring an urgent scan — and that, even if they had acted sooner, her prognosis would not have changed.

This response is profoundly disappointing. If my mother’s symptoms and test results had been properly assessed and monitored during her appointments, her condition could have been identified much earlier. She could have been placed on the appropriate treatment plan and spared the trauma of discovering her diagnosis only after reaching the A&E.
